## Trade Picker 1.7.2

Now on Minecraft 1.21, 1.21.1 and 1.21.11, and on NeoForge for 26.3 and 1.21.1. Adds picks for stew effects and dye colours, keeps trades in the order you choose them, and makes the picker faster.

### New

- **More Minecraft versions.** Fabric builds for 1.21–1.21.1 and 1.21.11, alongside 26.1–26.3.
- **NeoForge for 26.3 and 1.21.1.** This includes a Config button in the mod list. Villagers hold their rank until you pick its trades, the same as on Fabric. (#19)
- **Pick the exact variant.** A farmer's suspicious stew shows one card per effect, and a leatherworker's dyed leather shows one card per colour. (#14)
- **Trades appear in the order you pick them.** Selected cards are numbered 1, 2, and so on, and the villager lists the trades in that order. (#23)

### Changed

- **Faster picker.** The picker opens and confirms with less work per click. Settings save once, when you close the config screen. (#20)
- **Translatable screens.** The picker, the Reset button and the reset confirmation use translation keys. Enchantment and effect names come from Minecraft itself, so they are localised and modded ones display correctly. Professions show as "Farmer" rather than "FARMER". Tipped arrows show potency and duration, for example "Strength II (0:11)". (#21)
- **Picker screen polish.** Your selections, search text and scroll position survive a window or GUI-scale change. Search matches trade contents only, not the annotation text. (#18)

### Fixed

- **Correct enchanted-book labels with datapacks.** Librarians from datapack trade sets now show the enchantment you will actually get. (#16)
- **Book prices.** A picked enchanted book costs what its card showed, including single-level books such as Mending and Silk Touch. (#15)
- **Vanilla refusals.** As in vanilla, you can't trade with a sleeping or dying villager, or with one another player is already trading with. (#10)
- **Esc on the reset confirmation** goes back to the trade screen.
- **Walking away mid-pick** now shows a message saying your picks weren't applied.
- **Server-side checks.** The server validates every pick a client sends and rejects modified or out-of-range requests. (#9)

### Downloads

## Trade Picker 1.5.1

Adds Minecraft 26.3. Villagers now take a new rank only after you've picked its trades.

### Changed

- **Ranks wait for your picks.** A villager that earned its next rank used to take it on its own. It arrived with vanilla's random trades and no picker, and a long trading session could skip ranks entirely. Now the rank waits until you've chosen its trades, then arrives with them, one rank at a time.

### Fixed

- **Name tags and spawn eggs work on villagers again.** Right-clicking a villager with a named name tag names it, and using a villager spawn egg on it spawns a baby, as in vanilla.
- **No black flash when a screen opens.** The picker and the trade screen open straight over the world. Confirming your picks goes directly to the next screen without dropping back to the world first.

### If you played 1.5.0 (#25)

1.5.0 could leave a villager one rank short for good. A rank with nothing to choose, such as the librarian's Master rank, was filled in automatically but never granted. 1.5.1 grants those ranks. A villager that 1.5.0 already left stuck gets its rank the next time you right-click it, with no picker and no lost trades.

## Trade Picker 1.4.0

Curing a zombie villager now keeps everything you set up on it — your picked trades, your claim on the villager, and your discount.

### Fixed

- **Cured villagers keep the trades you picked.** Curing a zombie villager replaces it with a new entity behind the scenes, which detached it from your picks. The villager came back selling trades you never chose, and the picker never opened for it again. Your picks and your claim now follow a villager through the whole zombify-and-cure round trip.
- **Reputation discounts actually reach the trade screen.** Discounts from curing a villager, and from Hero of the Village, were being applied and then wiped a moment before the screen opened, so you saw the full price every time. They now show correctly on every open.
- **Villagers keep their picks through a Nether portal.** (#12) Profiles were stored per dimension, so a villager carried through a portal read as unclaimed on the far side and could be re-picked or reset by anyone. Profiles are now stored once for the whole world, and profiles saved by older versions are folded into the shared store automatically.
- **Trade use-counts no longer roll back after a reload.** (#11) Trades a villager already had before you installed the mod could reset their use counts when the world reloaded, restocking them early.
- **One unreadable profile no longer takes the rest down with it.** (#13) A single malformed entry stopped every villager profile in the world from loading. Bad entries are now skipped one at a time.
- **Cost scaling applies to tipped-arrow trades.** (#17) The fletcher's tipped-arrow trades ignored the cost-scaling setting.

## Trade Picker 1.3.2

Fixes a crash when trading with a villager on **Minecraft 1.21.11**. This build covers the whole **1.21.9 – 1.21.11** range in one jar.

### Fixed

- Trading with a villager on 1.21.11 crashed the server with a `NoSuchMethodError`. Two Minecraft APIs changed on 1.21.11 (a villager-trade method and the permission-level check); this release detects which version is running and calls the right one, so no separate download is needed for 1.21.11.

Closes #8.

## Trade Picker 1.3.1

Quality-of-life update for the trade picker, based on player feedback (#7).

### New
- **Already-picked trades are marked.** Trades a villager already sells show a green check mark and a note in the tooltip, so you never have to remember which trades you chose at earlier levels.
- **Hide Already-Picked Trades setting.** Turn it on to remove those trades from the picker entirely — you only see trades you don't have yet. Found in the mod settings (ModMenu). Off by default.
- **Sorted picker.** Trades are now sorted by type: regular trades first, then enchanted books and enchanted gear grouped alphabetically by enchantment and level. No more hunting through the list.
